confirmed.title: reconcile() is account-blind: it pushes the previous account's local projects into the newly signed-in user's cloud (shared-device cross-account leak)
confirmed.detail:
`reconcile(ownerId)` reads `metaAll = await meta.listSyncMeta()` (line 126) and then treats the mere *presence* of a meta record as "this project is already adopted by the current user". The trailing "locals the server doesn't know" loop at lines 209-218 does `if (!remoteById.has(l.id) && metaAll[l.id]) await pushTracked(l.id)` — it never compares `metaAll[l.id].ownerId` against the `ownerId` reconcile was called with. There is no ownerId check anywhere in reconcile, on any branch.

Sign-out does not clear local data: `useSignout` (frontend/src/auth/useAuth.js:46-55) only drops SIGNED_IN_HINT_KEY and nulls the react-query ME_KEY cache; the `projectStore` and `syncMeta` localForage stores are untouched, and nothing outside tests resets them (`_resetAllProjectStorageForTests` at projectStore.js:187 and `_resetSyncMetaForTests` at syncMeta.js:39 have no production callers). So both `manifest:{id}` and `sync-meta:{id}` records survive an account switch on the same browser profile.

Failure scenario (school lab / shared classroom PC — exactly the deployment the spec targets): Student A signs in on machine M; `reconcile(A)` pulls A's cloud projects into IndexedDB and writes `sync-meta:{P} = {ownerId: A}` (lines 181-187). A signs out (local data untouched). Student B signs in on the same browser. SyncProvider (SyncProvider.js:47) calls `engine.reconcile(B.id)`. B's `/api/projects` list does not contain A's ids, `suspectEmptyLocalIndex` is false because the local list is non-empty, so for every one of A's projects the loop at line 210 sees `!remoteById.has(P) && metaAll[P]` (truthy — it is A's meta) and calls `pushTracked(P)`, PUTting A's full manifest to `/api/projects/P` under **B's** session. The owner-scoped backend's (ownerId, id) primary key happily creates the row under B. A's entire project library is now stored in B's cloud account, visible to B, syncing down to every device B signs into, and exposed to anyone with teacher visibility over B. The leak is symmetric: B's cloud projects were imported to disk at lines 181-187, so when A signs back in the same loop uploads B's projects into A's account. It also silently bypasses the spec §3.2 consent prompt — those projects are excluded from the guest-import offer precisely *because* they have meta (SyncProvider.js:86) — and breaches spec §8.1 ("every project belongs to a named account") and the plan's Ownership constraint.

Secondary contributor at the same root: `getGlobalSyncEngine()` (lines 246-266) caches one engine for the page's whole lifetime, so the module-level `pending` Set built up under account A is still populated when B signs in — `onOnline`'s `drainPending()` (SyncProvider.js:132) pushes A's parked ids under B's session too. `pushOne` then writes meta back with `ownerId: (await meta.getSyncMeta(id))?.ownerId ?? null` (lines 31 and 37), preserving A's ownerId, so B's own later saves to those ids are silently skipped by the SyncProvider owner guard — B ends up with an un-syncing copy of A's work.

The implementer clearly knew about this hazard: SyncProvider.js:102 and :120 both guard with `if (meta.ownerId && meta.ownerId !== me.id) return; // another account's project`, and the plan's Global Constraints and Task 6/7 text say "owner-mismatched meta is skipped". reconcile — which runs on every sign-in, focus and online event — is the one path that omits the check, and no test in frontend/src/utils/sync/__tests__/syncEngine.test.js exercises a cross-owner meta, so nothing catches it.
confirmed.suggestedFix: Gate every meta-driven branch in `reconcile(ownerId)` on ownership, mirroring SyncProvider's idiom: add `const ownedMeta = (id) => { const mm = metaAll[id]; return mm && (!mm.ownerId || mm.ownerId === ownerId) ? mm : null; };` and require it at line 210 (`if (!remoteById.has(l.id) && ownedMeta(l.id))`) and likewise at lines 153, 166 and 173 (the delete-inference branch, the tombstone-apply branch, and the first loop's pushTracked). A local project whose meta names a different owner must be treated as not-adopted: never auto-pushed, never auto-deleted, left strictly local — and ideally routed into the §3.2 guest-import offer so the new user explicitly opts in. Also fix `pushOne` (lines 31 and 37) to stamp `ownerId` with the pushing user's id rather than re-reading and preserving the stale one, so meta never claims an owner different from where the row actually lives on the server. Finally, give the engine a `reset()` / `resetForAccount()` that clears `pending` and resets status, and have SyncProvider call it when `me.id` changes and on sign-out, so a previous account's pending ids can never drain under a new session. Add a regression test: local project with meta `{ownerId:"u-A"}` absent from u-B's remote list, `reconcile("u-B")` → no PUT issued.
confirmed.verifyReasoning:
The finding is fully corroborated by the current code.

1. `reconcile(ownerId)` in frontend/src/utils/sync/syncEngine.js has no ownerId check on any of its meta-driven branches. The "locals the server doesn't know" loop (lines 208-218) is exactly as quoted: `if (!remoteById.has(l.id) && metaAll[l.id]) { ... pushTracked(l.id) }` — it only checks that meta exists, never that `metaAll[l.id].ownerId === ownerId`. Same pattern (no ownerId check) exists in the tombstone branch (153/166) and the not-local-but-known branch (173).

2. Sign-out (frontend/src/auth/useAuth.js:46-55, `useSignout`) only removes `SIGNED_IN_HINT_KEY` from localStorage and nulls the react-query `ME_KEY` cache — it never touches projectStore or syncMeta local storage. Confirmed by reading the file directly.

3. The two reset helpers (`_resetAllProjectStorageForTests`, `_resetSyncMetaForTests`) are called only from test files (`__tests__/projectStore.test.js`, `__tests__/syncMeta.test.js`) — grep across the repo shows zero production callers, so nothing clears local IndexedDB/localForage state on account switch.

4. SyncProvider.js explicitly performs the ownerId-mismatch guard the finding says is missing from reconcile: line 102 (`if (meta && meta.ownerId && meta.ownerId !== me.id) return;`) in the save handler and line 120 in the delete handler — but reconcile is invoked at lines 47, 129, and 133 with no equivalent protection inside the engine itself, exactly the asymmetry the finding describes.

5. The backend PUT /api/projects/:id handler (backend/src/routes/projects.ts) scopes its "existing" lookup by `eq(projects.ownerId, req.user!.id)` and, finding no row, inserts a new row with `ownerId: req.user!.id` — i.e., whichever session's cookie is attached to the PUT request becomes the owner of that project row server-side. This confirms the concrete leak mechanism: engine.reconcile(B.id) calling pushTracked on A's project id, using B's authenticated session, creates/overwrites that project under B's account.

6. No test in syncEngine.test.js exercises a meta record whose ownerId differs from the ownerId reconcile is called with — every `metaMap.set` in that file uses `ownerId: "u-1"` while tests call `reconcile("u-1")`, confirming the gap is untested.

7. Cross-checked against `.superpowers/sdd/2026-08-19-classroom-platform-04-sync/final-review-rulings-and-minors.md`: Task 6's rulings/minors cover delete-inference containment, tombstone-recency, pending/retry, and status aggregation, but none of them mention an ownerId guard in reconcile or a cross-account leak — this is not a restatement of an existing ruling or deferred minor.

The finding's failure scenario (shared-device sign-in as A, sign-out, sign-in as B, reconcile(B.id) pushing A's untouched local projects/meta into B's cloud account under B's session) is reproducible directly from the code as it stands. This is a real, new, merge-blocking critical finding, not refuted.

confirmed.title: A sync pull into the currently-open project is invisible and is silently reverted by the next autosave (onProjectSaved subscriber refreshes only the list)
confirmed.detail:
The subscriber added for sync wiring ignores its `(manifest, opts)` arguments and only calls `refreshList()` (ProjectContext.js:97-99). Its delete twin at lines 100-104 correctly closes an open project that was tombstoned remotely, but the save twin never updates `activeManifest`, and nothing re-applies the pulled manifest into SimulationContext. Sync pulls go straight through `projectStore.saveProject(project.manifest, {preserveTimestamp:true})` (syncEngine.js:182 and :193), bypassing `persistActive` — so localForage and the start-menu list hold the new content while `activeManifest` and the editor still hold the old one.

Failure scenario: Device B has project P open in the IDE. Device A edits P and pushes (server head now t2, content Y). B's window regains focus → `onFocus` → `reconcile` → `r.clientUpdatedAt (t2) > local.updatedAt (t1)` → GET + `saveProject(Y, {preserveTimestamp:true})`. IndexedDB now holds Y, but `proj.activeManifest` is still the t1 manifest X and the editor still renders X — the user is never shown that a newer version arrived. (Same shape when a student restores a stale tab at home and opens the project before/while the initial or focus reconcile lands.) The autosave dirty-check in frontend/src/hooks/useProject.js:82-87 compares `sim.*` against that stale `activeManifest`, reports `unchanged`, and stays quiet, so the divergence persists. The moment the student types one character, the dirty-check schedules an autosave, `saveCurrent` → `captureWorkingStateInto(proj.activeManifest)` (useProject.js:56) spreads the STALE base — so `runs`, `datasets` and every other field from Y are dropped too — stamps `updatedAt: Date.now()`, and `persistActive` overwrites Y locally. SyncProvider's onProjectSaved then pushes it; the server sees a strictly newer ms, archives Y as reason `overwrite`, and makes X-plus-one-keystroke the head on every device. Device A's work disappears from the whole system with no user-visible signal, inverting most-recent-wins and recoverable only from `project_versions`, which has no UI on this branch (Task 3 ruling deferred the restore screen).

This is the core two-device edit case the plan exists to serve, and the pull path's `preserveTimestamp` correctness work is nullified by it.
confirmed.suggestedFix: Have the subscriber use its arguments and adopt sync-applied writes to the open project: `onProjectSaved((manifest, opts) => { refreshList().catch(() => {}); if (opts?.preserveTimestamp && manifest?.id === activeProjectIdRef.current) setActiveManifest(manifest); })` (use a ref for the id to avoid re-subscribing). Updating `activeManifest` alone is not enough — the dirty-check would then see sim != manifest and re-save the stale sim state — so also push the pulled manifest into working state: expose a callback from useProject's `applyManifestToWorkingState` and re-run it when the active manifest is replaced by a pull, cancelling the pending debounced autosave first (`debouncedSaveRef.current.cancel()`) so an in-flight stale save cannot land after the pull. If overwriting a student's on-screen editor state is judged too abrupt, the minimum acceptable behaviour is to surface the pulled version ("this project was updated on another device — reload it") rather than let it be silently clobbered.
confirmed.verifyReasoning:
Verified every link in the claimed causal chain against the current code:

1. ProjectContext.js:97-99 — `onProjectSaved((manifest, opts) => ...)` subscriber genuinely discards both arguments and only calls `refreshList()`. Confirmed by reading the file directly; matches the delete twin at 100-104 which correctly does act on its arguments.

2. syncEngine.js:182 and :193 — both the "new remote project" and "remote newer than local" branches of `reconcile()` call `store.saveProject(project.manifest, { preserveTimestamp: true })` directly, bypassing ProjectContext's `persistActive`. Line numbers match exactly.

3. projectStore.js saveProject (line 105-125) stamps and writes to localForage, then synchronously calls every `saveListeners` subscriber with `(stamped, opts)` — so the pulled manifest and `{preserveTimestamp:true}` do reach ProjectContext's subscriber, which ignores them.

4. SyncProvider.js confirms `window.addEventListener("focus", onFocus)` → `engine.reconcile(me.id)` (line 129, 136), and its own `onProjectSaved` handler explicitly skips re-pushing when `opts?.preserveTimestamp` (line 100) — consistent with the finding's framing of a "pull path."

5. useProject.js's dirty-check effect (lines 74-96) compares live `sim.*` fields only against `proj.activeManifest` — since that stays stale after a pull, the check reports "unchanged" and does nothing until the user edits. The very next edit's autosave calls `captureWorkingStateInto(proj.activeManifest)` (line 56, using the stale base), which spreads the stale manifest and stamps a fresh `updatedAt`, then `persistActive` overwrites the newer pulled content locally with a manifest based on stale data.

6. SyncProvider's own `onProjectSaved` handler then pushes that stale-based save (no `preserveTimestamp`), which server-side is a strictly newer timestamp overwriting the true latest — this matches Task 2's documented ruling that differing-content newer timestamps win and archive the old head with reason "overwrite."

7. No other code path (grepped for `activeManifest`/`openProject`/`selectProject` usage repo-wide) re-applies a sync-pulled manifest into the open project's `activeManifest` or into `SimulationContext` — IDELayout.js only reads `proj.activeManifest`, it never intercepts pulls.

8. Checked `.superpowers/sdd/2026-08-19-classroom-platform-04-sync/final-review-rulings-and-minors.md` in full (46 lines) — no ruling or deferred minor addresses this specific save-pull-into-open-project gap. The closest items (dirty-check-must-not-restamp-on-open ruling, and the onProjectDeleted-listener ruling) are adjacent but do not cover or dispose of this scenario; this is a new, real, merge-blocking defect matching the finding's exact causal chain and line citations.

Every concrete step of the failure scenario reproduces against the code as it currently exists, with accurate file/line citations throughout. The finding is real.

confirmed.title: Sign-out leaves every cloud-pulled project and its sync-meta on disk, exposing one student's work to the next user of a shared device
confirmed.detail:
Before this branch, local IndexedDB only ever held projects created on that device. Plan 4 adds a cloud pull: `reconcile()` writes every remote project the account owns into the shared browser profile (`store.saveProject(project.manifest, {preserveTimestamp:true})`, syncEngine.js:182 and :193) plus a sync-meta record for each. `useSignout().onSuccess` (lines 50-53) clears only the SIGNED_IN_HINT_KEY and the react-query `me` cache; `AccountChip`'s handler (frontend/src/components/auth/AccountChip.js:47-51) just awaits that mutation and navigates to "/". No code path clears `projectStore` or `syncMeta` on sign-out or on account change — `_resetAllProjectStorageForTests` (projectStore.js:187) and `_resetSyncMetaForTests` (syncMeta.js:39) are test-only and have no production callers.

Failure scenario: a student signs into the school-lab browser to check one assignment. Their whole cloud project library is downloaded to that machine. They sign out and leave. The next student opens the IDE as a guest (or signs into their own account) and sees the previous student's projects listed in the start menu, and can open, read, edit and export every one of them. On a K-12 platform with a hard 200-user cap and shared lab hardware this is a systematic, per-sign-in privacy exposure introduced by this branch, and it is also the precondition that makes the cross-account reconcile upload reachable.
confirmed.suggestedFix: On sign-out (and on detecting that `me.id` changed from a previously-recorded id), clear the cloud-derived local state: delete every `manifest:{id}` whose sync-meta names the departing owner, delete those sync-meta records, and refresh the project list — leaving genuinely local/guest projects (no meta) alone. Record the last signed-in user id in localStorage so an account switch that skips the sign-out button (session expiry, a different account signing in directly) is caught too. If a full wipe is judged too aggressive for the local-first promise, at minimum gate the start-menu listing so projects whose meta names a different owner are not shown while a different (or no) user is signed in.
confirmed.verifyReasoning:
Traced the full code path and confirmed every claim in the finding against current code:

1. syncEngine.reconcile() (frontend/src/utils/sync/syncEngine.js, lines 181-187 and 191-198) pulls every remote project owned by the signed-in account into the local projectStore (localForage/IndexedDB) via store.saveProject(project.manifest, {preserveTimestamp:true}) and writes a matching sync-meta record — exactly as cited.
2. useSignout().onSuccess (frontend/src/auth/useAuth.js lines 50-53) only does localStorage.removeItem(SIGNED_IN_HINT_KEY) and qc.setQueryData(ME_KEY, null) — it never touches projectStore or syncMeta.
3. AccountChip's sign-out button handler (frontend/src/components/auth/AccountChip.js lines 47-51) just awaits signout.mutateAsync() and navigates to "/" — no cleanup call.
4. SyncProvider's effect cleanup (frontend/src/sync/SyncProvider.js lines 139-151), which runs on sign-out/account-change (effect keyed on me?.id), only clears the guest-import-prompt UI state — it does not wipe cloud-pulled projects or their sync-meta.
5. projectStore.listProjects() (frontend/src/utils/storage/projectStore.js lines 69-73) returns every stored project summary with zero ownership/session filtering; ProjectContext.refreshList (contexts/ProjectContext.js lines 41-45) feeds this straight into projectList, and StartMenu.js renders projectList verbatim in the "Continue" list — no filter by current signed-in user or syncMeta.ownerId anywhere in that chain.
6. _resetAllProjectStorageForTests (projectStore.js) and _resetSyncMetaForTests (syncMeta.js) are confirmed test-only via grep — no production file calls either.

So the concrete failure scenario (student A signs in on a shared lab machine, cloud pull writes all their projects to that browser's IndexedDB, they sign out, student B opens the IDE as guest or signs into their own account and sees/opens/edits/exports student A's full project library in the start menu) is reproducible exactly as described in the current code — nothing filters the start-menu list by owner and nothing clears cloud-pulled state on sign-out.

I also checked whether this was already surfaced/accepted: final-review-rulings-and-minors.md (Task 6/7/9 sections covering sync/guest-import) contains no ruling or deferred-minor entry about clearing local state on sign-out or shared-device exposure — it's not mentioned at all. The implementation plan (docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-19-classroom-platform-04-sync.md line 1846) explicitly scoped useSignout's onSuccess to only removing SIGNED_IN_HINT_KEY, confirming this is a genuine plan/spec gap that was carried through to final review, not a deviation that was caught and ruled on. The product spec (docs/classroom-platform.md line 24: "work belongs to someone and follows them between computers") confirms multi-device same-account usage is an explicit design goal, which is precisely the mechanism that makes this exposure reachable, and the platform explicitly targets K-12 classrooms with a 200-user cap where shared/lab computers are a realistic deployment pattern.

This is a real, novel, merge-blocking privacy defect, not a restatement of an accepted ruling or deferred minor. The finding should stand.

confirmed.title: Autosave debounce is only cancelled on unmount, so a pending timer from the previous project restamps updatedAt on the project you just opened
confirmed.detail: `debouncedSaveRef.current` is cancelled only by the unmount cleanup (useProject.js:97); nothing cancels it when the active project changes. `saveCurrentRef.current` is refreshed on every render (useProject.js:63-65), so a timer scheduled while project A was open fires against whatever is active when it expires. Failure scenario (MANIFEST_AUTOSAVE_MS = 3000, constants/index.js:37): the user types in project A, and within 3s clicks project B in the start menu. `selectProject` (useProject.js:99) saves A correctly, opens B, and applies B to sim, so the dirty-check effect at lines 74-96 sees `unchanged === true` and schedules nothing — but A's timer is still armed. ~3s later it calls `saveCurrent()` now bound to B: `captureWorkingStateInto(B)` sets `updatedAt: Date.now()` and `persistActive` → `saveProject` restamps again, then `onProjectSaved` fires and SyncProvider pushes B. This is exactly the behaviour the dirty-check ruling exists to prevent ("opening a project must not restamp"): if this device's copy of B is stale (edited on another machine, focus-reconcile hasn't run yet), B now claims `updatedAt = now` and the next push wins most-recent-wins, demoting the genuinely newer server head to an archived version — violating spec docs/classroom-platform.md:215 ("the most recent edit wins"), and with the student-facing history/restore screen deferred there is no UI to get it back. `createNew()` has the same leftover-timer window.
confirmed.suggestedFix: Cancel the pending debounce when the active project changes, e.g. add `useEffect(() => () => debouncedSaveRef.current.cancel(), [proj.activeProjectId])` (declared before the dirty-check effect so its cleanup runs first), or make the debounced callback capture the project id it was scheduled for and no-op when `proj.activeProjectId` no longer matches.
confirmed.verifyReasoning:
I read frontend/src/hooks/useProject.js in full and traced the exact mechanism the finding describes:

1. Lines 66-73: `debouncedSaveRef.current` is created once via `debounce(() => saveCurrentRef.current?.(), MANIFEST_AUTOSAVE_MS)`. `saveCurrentRef` is refreshed every render (lines 62-65), so whichever `saveCurrent` closure exists when the timer fires is the one used — bound to whatever project is active at fire time, not at schedule time.
2. Lines 74-96: the dirty-check effect schedules `debouncedSaveRef.current()` only when sim state differs from `proj.activeManifest`. This effect has no cleanup function.
3. Line 97: the only cancellation is in a separate effect with `[]` deps — fires solely on unmount, never on `proj.activeProjectId` change.
4. `debounce()` (frontend/src/utils/debounce.js) is a standard trailing-edge debounce: calling the debounced function again resets the timer, but *not* calling it again leaves a previously armed timer running untouched.
5. `selectProject` (lines 99-116): awaits `saveCurrent()` synchronously for the outgoing project (this save is fine), then opens and applies the new project. The dirty-check effect re-runs, sees `unchanged === true` for the freshly-applied project, and does NOT call `debouncedSaveRef.current()` again — so it neither reschedules nor cancels the old timer armed while the previous project was being edited.
6. When that stale timer fires (~3s after being armed), it calls the *current* `saveCurrentRef.current()`, which now closes over the *new* active project/manifest, and calls `proj.persistActive(next)` → `saveProject`.
7. `saveProject` (frontend/src/utils/storage/projectStore.js:105-125) unconditionally restamps `updatedAt: Date.now()` unless `opts.preserveTimestamp` is passed (it isn't, here), and fires `onProjectSaved` listeners.
8. `SyncProvider`'s `onProjectSaved` handler (frontend/src/sync/SyncProvider.js) checks `opts?.preserveTimestamp` (false here) and calls `engine.pushProject(id)`, pushing the now-restamped manifest to the server.
9. Backend `projects.ts` (lines ~170-224) resolves push conflicts purely by comparing `m.updatedAt` (client) against `head.clientUpdatedAt` (server): if incoming `updatedAt` is not less than the server head's, the server archives the PREVIOUS head and accepts the incoming version — i.e., a stale local copy restamped to `Date.now()` can win over and archive a genuinely newer version saved from another device, exactly matching the "most-recent-wins" mechanism described in docs/classroom-platform.md:215.

This reproduces the finding's exact failure scenario end-to-end: type in A → switch to B within the 3s window → dirty-check sees B as unchanged and schedules nothing → A's leftover timer fires anyway, now bound to B → B gets restamped and pushed even though nothing in B changed, risking demotion of a genuinely newer server copy of B.

I also checked .superpowers/sdd/2026-08-19-classroom-platform-04-sync/final-review-rulings-and-minors.md. Its one relevant ruling ("autosave dirty-check against activeManifest — opening a project must not restamp") addresses a different failure mode — the dirty-check effect itself misfiring when a project is merely *opened* (which is exactly what the current `unchanged` check at lines 82-87 was built to fix) — not the separate leftover-timer-survives-project-switch bug the finding identifies. No test file for useProject exists, and no ruling or deferred minor covers this specific scenario, so it is not a restatement of an already-accepted/deferred item.

The finding is accurate, reproducible in the code as it exists now, and has genuine data-integrity impact (spurious restamp-and-push able to demote a real newer version, with no restore UI per the deferred history/restore screen). It should stand.

confirmed.title: Server cap/oversize/validation sentences are discarded — the plan's "client surfaces the server sentence verbatim" constraint is unimplemented
confirmed.detail:
The plan's Global Constraints (Caps, docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-19-classroom-platform-04-sync.md:21) end with "All checked server-side; the client surfaces the server sentence verbatim." Nothing on the client does. `api()` builds an `ApiError` carrying the exact sentence (frontend/src/utils/api/client.js:27-31), but `pushProject`'s catch (syncEngine.js:70-75) reads only `err?.status` to guess offline and then throws the error away (no message kept, not even a console.warn); `deleteRemoteProject` (line 106) catches with no binding at all; `reconcile` only `console.warn`s it. The engine status object carries only `{state, pendingCount}`. The single sync surface, SyncChip, is a fixed 5-entry label map (SyncChip.js:5-11) rendered at line 36 with a hardcoded reassurance `title` (line 35). Three of the four byte-exact backend sentences — `You've reached the 100-project limit — delete something first.`, `This project is too large to sync. Export it as a file instead.`, `That doesn't look like a valid project.` — exist nowhere in frontend/src (grep confirms zero occurrences outside a backend-fake in syncEngine.test.js), and no component reads a sync error message. This is the item the controller explicitly deferred to final-review triage (rulings file, Task 6 minor: "F1-revive can hit the PUT cap outcome and park in pending with no backoff/user explanation (UX, final review to triage)"), and it is not in the plan's Deferred list.

Failure scenario: a Grade-11 student's manifest crosses 400 KB (very reachable — charts plus run snapshots; the plan itself names run-trace externalization as deferred and says "the 400 KB cap is the guard"). Every 3 s autosave fires a PUT that 413s with the actionable sentence; the id parks in `pending`; the chip reads "Saved on this computer · Sync error" with the tooltip "Your work saves locally first and syncs to your account." The student is never told the project is too large, never told to export it, and silently loses spec §6.3's "start at school and continue at home" for that project — and because the id stays in `pending` the >400 KB body is re-uploaded on every save and every online/focus event forever, with no backoff. Same for the 101st project (403) and the 400 "That doesn't look like a valid project.", and for a guest-import accept that hits the cap (SyncProvider.js:165 swallows it into a console.warn and re-shows the banner with no reason). All three permanent failures are indistinguishable from a transient network blip.
confirmed.suggestedFix: Carry the server sentence through unmodified: in `pushProject`/`adoptLocalProject`/`deleteRemoteProject`/`reconcile`, when the error is an `ApiError` (or `err.status` is 400/403/413) keep `err.message` on the status object (e.g. `setStatus({state:"error", message: err.message})`) — never paraphrased, never wrapped, so the four sentences stay byte-exact. Render it in SyncChip: `title={status.message ?? default}` at minimum, and for permanent 4xx a visible line beside/below the "· Sync error" label; show it in the GuestImportPrompt failure path too. Additionally, do not re-queue ids whose push failed with a permanent 4xx into `pending`, so a doomed 400 KB PUT is not retried on every save and every online event.
confirmed.verifyReasoning:
I read the current code and could reproduce essentially all of the finding's claims.

Confirmed against current code:
- frontend/src/utils/api/client.js:27-31 — ApiError.message carries the server's exact `data.error` string.
- frontend/src/utils/sync/syncEngine.js: `pushProject`'s catch (lines 70-75) reads only `err?.status`/`navigator.onLine` and discards `err`/`err.message` entirely — only `{state}` is set. `deleteRemoteProject`'s catch (line 106) is a bare `catch {}`, no binding at all. `reconcile`'s per-item catches (204, 213) and its outer try/catch (133) only `console.warn` or set `state:"error"` — message never retained. The public status object is built solely from `{state, pendingCount}` (setStatus, line 13-14) — there is no field to carry a message.
- frontend/src/sync/SyncChip.js: a fixed 5-entry `LABELS` map (idle/synced/syncing/offline/error) and a hardcoded `title` "Your work saves locally first and syncs to your account." (line 35) — no per-state or per-error message is ever rendered.
- Grepped `frontend/` for the three byte-exact sentences ("100-project limit", "too large to sync", "doesn't look like a valid project") — zero matches anywhere in frontend, including the test file (the finding's claim that a fake copy exists in a test file is actually itself wrong — there isn't even that; the sentences are entirely absent from the frontend). This makes the underlying point (nothing on the client ever surfaces these) even more true, not less.
- Plan doc (docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-19-classroom-platform-04-sync.md:21) does say verbatim: "All checked server-side; the client surfaces the server sentence verbatim." — a real, written, unambiguous plan constraint that is not implemented.
- Retry-forever mechanism checked and confirmed: `pending` doesn't distinguish permanent (4xx) from transient failures; `onProjectSaved` in SyncProvider.js calls `engine.pushProject(manifest.id)` on every autosave, and `drainPending`/`reconcile` re-fire on every online/focus event — so a permanently oversize/capped project is genuinely re-PUT forever with no backoff, which is a real correctness defect beyond pure UX polish.

One inaccuracy I found in the finding: the guest-import sub-scenario ("SyncProvider.js:165 swallows it into a console.warn and re-shows the banner with no reason") mischaracterizes the mechanism — `pushProject` never rethrows (it catches internally and only sets status), so `adoptLocalProject` doesn't throw on an API-level cap failure either; the `handleAcceptImport` catch at line 169-174 would not fire for this case. In reality the banner would silently auto-dismiss as if the import succeeded, while the push quietly parks in `pending`/`error` — arguably worse than what's described, but the finding's stated mechanism for that particular example is wrong. This is a secondary supporting example, not the core scenario, so it doesn't undercut the primary claim (autosave-triggered PUT hitting the 413/403/400 cap and silently discarding the sentence).

On the "restates a deferred minor" disqualifier: rulings-and-minors.md Task 6 does contain "F1-revive can hit the PUT cap outcome and park in pending with no backoff/user explanation (UX, final review to triage)". But that minor is scoped narrowly to one code path (tombstone-revive) and framed as a UX nicety explicitly punted to this very final-review pass for a decision — it is not itself a resolution. This finding is materially broader (all three cap/oversize/invalid-shape sentences, across pushProject/adoptLocalProject/deleteRemoteProject/reconcile, i.e. the normal autosave path too, not just revive) and identifies an unambiguous unimplemented plan requirement plus a genuine forever-retry defect. That is new, verified, merge-blocking-relevant substance rather than a mere restatement, and it lands exactly where the triage note said it should.

Given the finding's central technical claims are all reproducible in the current code, the cited plan constraint is real and unmet, and the scope/impact exceeds the narrow already-noted minor, I am not refuting this finding (only flagging the one inaccurate sub-example above for the reviewer's awareness).

confirmed.title: Welcome playground animates forever regardless of prefers-reduced-motion, with no stop control
confirmed.detail: Task 10's behavioral contract says "animation is CSS keyframes + one IntersectionObserver + one requestAnimationFrame canvas; `prefers-reduced-motion` disables the decorative motion" (plan line ~1927). The CSS honours it for the orbit and the reveal transitions (styles.css:4490-4494), but the canvas loop does not: the effect at GravityPlayground.js:25-57 unconditionally starts `requestAnimationFrame(frame)` and re-arms itself every frame, and the balls never come to rest (every wall/floor hit reflects with DAMPING 0.82 and the floor bounce uses `-Math.abs(vy)`, so motion continues indefinitely). Setting the gravity slider to 0 does not stop it either — it leaves the balls travelling at constant velocity, still bouncing off the walls. Failure scenario: a motion-sensitive student or teacher with "Reduce motion" enabled at the OS level opens the app for the first time, is redirected to `/welcome` (the mandatory brand-new-visitor path), scrolls to "Feel it work", and gets a permanently animating 260 px canvas of bouncing balls with no pause, stop, or hide mechanism anywhere on the page — the one screen every new user is forced through.
confirmed.suggestedFix: In GravityPlayground's effect, read `window.matchMedia?.("(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)")`; when it matches, render a single static frame (draw the initial balls once) and skip `requestAnimationFrame` entirely, and have `drop()` redraw statically rather than restarting the loop. Alternatively add a visible Pause/Play control that starts paused under reduced motion.
confirmed.verifyReasoning: Read GravityPlayground.js in full: the effect (lines 25-57) starts requestAnimationFrame unconditionally and the frame callback re-arms itself every tick with no matchMedia/prefers-reduced-motion check anywhere in the file (grep confirms the only prefers-reduced-motion reference in frontend/src is in styles.css, not in any JS). styles.css:4490-4494 only disables .welcome-orbit__path, .welcome-reveal, and .welcome-btn transitions — it cannot affect the canvas's imperative ctx.fill() drawing. Setting gravity to 0 does not stop the animation: vy is simply held constant (no force added) while balls continue moving and bouncing off walls (lines 45-47), since DAMPING only attenuates each bounce's outgoing speed rather than driving velocity to zero, and the horizontal-wall branches don't touch vy at all. WelcomePage.js renders <GravityPlayground/> in the mandatory /welcome page (Task 10 ruling confirms /welcome is shown to brand-new visitors) with no pause/stop control in either file's markup. Checked final-review-rulings-and-minors.md Task 10 entries — they cover the orbit CSS animation and redirect gating logic, not the canvas RAF motion-accessibility gap, so this is not a restated ruling or already-deferred minor. The finding's concrete failure scenario is reproducible in the code as it currently exists.

confirmed.title: Unguarded awaits in the wiring IIFE can kill push-after-save for the session while the chip still reads "Synced"
confirmed.detail: The file's own comments state the invariant twice — a failure here "would silently kill push-after-save for the whole session" (lines 74-80) — and the reconcile call is defensively try/caught for exactly that reason (lines 47-53). But three awaits in the same IIFE are outside any try/catch: `await getGlobalSyncEngine()` (line 33), `const locals = await listProjects()` (line 45), and `const metas = await listSyncMeta()` (line 85). A rejection at any of them aborts the IIFE before `onProjectSaved` (line 98) and `onProjectDeleted` (line 114) are ever registered, and there is no catch on the IIFE, so it also surfaces as an unhandled promise rejection in devtools. Failure scenario: a school-managed browser with IndexedDB blocked/erroring (or a stale tab whose lazily-imported chunk 404s after a redeploy) — `listProjects()` rejects, the subscriptions are never installed, so for the rest of the session nothing this signed-in student saves or deletes is ever pushed to their account, and no reconcile trigger repairs it because `engineRef.current` is set but the save hook is absent. Meanwhile SyncChip is still mounted, `me` is truthy, engine status is the initial `idle`, and LABELS maps `idle → "Synced"` (SyncChip.js:6, 36), so the status bar states "Saved on this computer · Synced" — the precise false reassurance spec §6.3 ("shows the truth at all times") exists to prevent. Note a naive `catch { }` here is not enough: continuing with an empty `guestIdsRef` would make the save handler auto-adopt every guest-era project (line 108), uploading guest work without the §3.2 offer.
confirmed.suggestedFix: Wrap the IIFE body (or at least the three awaits) in try/catch. On failure: (a) still register `onProjectSaved`/`onProjectDeleted`, but set a `provenanceUnknown` flag that makes the save handler treat "no meta" as guest-era so nothing is auto-adopted without the §3.2 offer; (b) push the engine into a non-synced status so the chip stops claiming "Synced"; (c) `console.warn` once, matching the existing idiom.
confirmed.verifyReasoning:
I read frontend/src/sync/SyncProvider.js in full and verified every concrete claim in the finding against the actual current code:

- Line 33 `const engine = await getGlobalSyncEngine();` is outside any try/catch. getGlobalSyncEngine() (syncEngine.js:253-266) does real dynamic imports (`../api/client`, storage modules) and can genuinely reject (e.g., a stale chunk 404 after redeploy).
- Line 45 `const locals = await listProjects();` sits between the getGlobalSyncEngine call and the `try { await engine.reconcile(...) }` block starting at line 46 — confirmed outside the try/catch. listProjects() (projectStore.js:69-73) calls localForage's `getItem`, which can reject on IndexedDB failures.
- Line 85 `const metas = await listSyncMeta();` is after the legacy-backfill try/catch closes (line 82) and is likewise unguarded.
- The whole wiring effect is a bare `(async () => {...})();` at line 127 with no trailing `.catch()`, so any of these three rejections both (a) aborts the function before `onProjectSaved` (line 98) and `onProjectDeleted` (line 114) are registered, and (b) surfaces as an unhandled promise rejection.
- Verified SyncChip.js independently: it calls its own `getGlobalSyncEngine()` (which returns the same cached, already-resolved promise if SyncProvider's line-33 call succeeded), defaults to `state: "idle"`, and LABELS maps `idle → "Synced"`. Confirmed createSyncEngine's initial status is literally `{ state: "idle", pendingCount: 0 }` (syncEngine.js:8), so nothing changes that unless reconcile/push actually runs — which never happens if listProjects() (line 45) throws before reconcile is even reached. This exactly reproduces the "false reassurance" scenario the finding describes: chip says "Synced" while push-after-save is permanently dead for the session.
- The suggested-fix caveat (a naive blanket catch would leave guestIdsRef empty, causing auto-adoption of guest-era projects on next save) is also correct given lines 20, 86, 91, 107-108.

I then checked whether this restates something already ruled on/deferred. final-review-rulings-and-minors.md and task-7-report.md show the team was well aware of exactly this failure class ("silently killing push-after-save for the whole session" is verbatim language from Task 7's Finding 2) but deliberately scoped the fix to wrap only the `reconcile` call ("the try/catch wraps exactly the `reconcile` call, nothing broader"). Neither that ruling, nor Task 9's deferred minor ("no disposed check between backfill awaits"), nor any other entry in the rulings file addresses the three specific awaits this finding flags (getGlobalSyncEngine at line 33, listProjects at line 45, listSyncMeta at line 85). This is a genuine gap left by an intentionally narrow prior fix, not a restatement of an accepted ruling or deferred minor, and it has real, reproducible, merge-relevant impact (false "Synced" status + silent session-long sync death) matching the project's own stated spec concern (§6.3 "shows the truth at all times"). The finding survives adversarial review.

minors: syncEngine.js:191-201 — equal-ms with differing content is a client no-op (neither pull nor push) while the server (projects.ts:192-198) treats ties as newer; device and server can stay divergent until the next local edit bumps the ms.

syncEngine.js:191-198 — the pull decision comes from the pre-GET `localList` snapshot and `saveProject(preserveTimestamp)` overwrites unconditionally; a local autosave that lands during a slow reconcile is destroyed with no archive anywhere (it was never pushed, so no `project_versions` row exists).

syncEngine.js:102-110 — `deleteRemoteProject` ignores the `online` flag: an offline delete reports state "error" rather than "offline" and has no pending queue, relying entirely on reconcile's delete-inference to retry.

projects.ts:69-79 — once `pruneTombstones` hard-deletes a tombstone (>100 deleted projects), other devices holding local copy + meta fall into syncEngine.js:210 and resurrect the project in the cloud; the tombstone bound and the delete-propagation mechanism are coupled.
SyncProvider.js:130-134 — `onOnline` fires `drainPending()` and `reconcile()` unawaited and concurrently; the same manifest can be pushed twice and the status transitions interleave.
SyncProvider.js:129 — reconcile runs on every window focus with no debounce or in-flight guard; overlapping reconciles are possible on a slow link.

projects.ts:303 — restore stamps the SERVER clock as `clientUpdatedAt`, while every other value in that column is a CLIENT clock; on a device whose clock runs ahead, an ordinary save made before the restore can still out-rank it on the next push.

syncEngine.js:31,37 — pushOne re-writes meta with `(await meta.getSyncMeta(id))?.ownerId ?? null`, preserving a stale/foreign ownerId instead of stamping the account that actually now holds the row; a project pushed by a second account keeps claiming the first. (Part of the Critical fix.)

syncEngine.js:153 and :173 — the tombstone-apply and delete-inference branches also key off `metaAll[r.id]` with no owner comparison; same class as the Critical finding, lower impact because it additionally needs a project-id collision across accounts.

backend/src/routes/projects.ts:95 — no route in the projects plugin carries `config.rateLimit`, and app.ts:32 registers @fastify/rate-limit with `global:false`; only auth routes are limited. A signed-in account can loop PUT/DELETE at full speed (consistent with classes/members/admin, so pre-existing pattern, but the new routes are the heaviest writes in the API).

Aggregate storage per account is unbounded in bytes: 100 live + 100 tombstoned projects, each with a 400 KB head plus up to 20 (21 after DELETE, which never prunes) 400 KB versions ≈ 1.7 GB — roughly 8x spec §428's "a couple of hundred MB — generous for real use, fatal for abuse". No byte-level accounting exists anywhere; the caps are count-based only.
backend/src/routes/projects.ts:269 — `logEvent("project.deleted")` writes to the append-only `events` table with no cap or prune, unlike tombstones; a create/delete loop grows `events` without bound.

backend/src/routes/projects.ts:163,218 — ManifestSchema.passthrough() accepts strings containing U+0000; Postgres jsonb rejects those (SQLSTATE 22P05), so such a manifest 500s inside the transaction instead of returning a 400.

backend/src/routes/projects.ts:107 — the scoped error handler's `reply.send(err)` fallback keeps Fastify's default of echoing `err.message` on 5xx, so Postgres error text (constraint names, type-cast failures) reaches the client. Matches the app-wide default, but these routes widen that surface.

backend/src/routes/projects.ts:37 — stableStringify recurses without a depth bound over attacker-controlled manifest structure, on the equal-ms tie path the client fully controls; a deeply nested manifest that survives JSON.parse can RangeError inside the PUT transaction and 500.
backend/src/routes/projects.ts:291 — GET .../versions exposes the globally-sequential bigserial `versionId`, letting any account estimate platform-wide write volume from gaps between its own ids.

backend/src/routes/projects.ts:128,248 — GET and DELETE /api/projects/:id do not apply PROJECT_ID_REGEX (only PUT does); harmless today since both are parameterized and owner-scoped, but the id-shape contract is enforced on one route out of five.

syncMeta.js and the `pide_guest_import_declined:{userId}` localStorage keys accumulate per-account records on a shared device, leaving an enumerable list of which user ids have signed in on that machine.

projectStore.js:187 `_resetAllProjectStorageForTests` clears the three localForage stores but NOT the `saveListeners`/`deleteListeners` registries, contradicting the deferred-minor note that claims listener-leak hygiene is handled there; a test that mounts SyncProvider and resets storage leaves live subscribers behind.

SyncProvider.js:16 `engineRef.current` is never nulled in the effect cleanup, so after sign-out a stale engine handle stays reachable from `handleAcceptImport`; harmless today only because the engine is a process-wide singleton.

SyncProvider.js:163-167 the accept loop has no `disposed`/`me.id` re-check between iterations: signing out mid-import keeps stamping `sync-meta{ownerId: <old account>}` on the remaining ids, which is precisely the state finding 1 later replays into the next account.

Two tabs on the same browser run two independent engines over one shared localForage: tab B never receives tab A's `onProjectSaved`/`onProjectDeleted` (they are in-process only), so tab B's in-memory `activeManifest` goes stale and its autosave/push can overwrite tab A's work; no storage-event or BroadcastChannel bridge exists.

WelcomePage.js:20 `go()` calls `localStorage.setItem(WELCOME_SEEN_KEY, ...)` before `navigate(path)`; if localStorage throws (quota/blocked), every CTA on /welcome becomes a no-op and the visitor is stuck on the welcome screen.

useProject.js:97 the unmount cleanup `cancel()`s rather than `flush()`es, discarding up to 3s of typing; benign for in-app route changes only because SimulationProvider/ProjectProvider sit above `<Routes>` in App.js and re-schedule on return.

Spec-fidelity sweep is otherwise clean: all four backend sentences are byte-exact (em dash U+2014 in the cap sentence verified), the §6.3 chip strings match the spec byte-for-byte (middle dot U+00B7 verified), §3.2's "Bring your N guest project(s) into your new account?" + [Bring them in]/[Not now] matches, caps are 100/400 KB/20 as specced, requireUser (not requireConfirmed) guards /api/projects*, SCHEMA_VERSION stays 2, sync-meta lives in its own localForage store, and only project.deleted/project.restored are logged.

Welcome-screen contract verified end to end: gate logic at WelcomeGate.js:7-10 matches the three-condition rule, grandfathering stamps the flag at line 29, all four CTAs (three hero + footer) stamp WELCOME_SEEN_KEY via go() in WelcomePage.js:20, /welcome is a plain route (App.js:50) unaffected by the `*` catch-all, and the IDE stays at "/".
The plan's Deferred list is honest — the student-facing history/restore screen is listed there and the Task 3 API did land; no other promised behavior is quietly missing.

SyncProvider.js:67-72 resurrects the legacy v1 blob for signed-in users but leaves bootstrapResult as {kind:"empty"}, so unlike the signed-out path (useProject.js:145) the recovered project is listed but never auto-opened — a silent behavioral divergence between the two resurrection paths.

reconcile's pull path (syncEngine.js:181-188) writes remote manifests into the one shared local store regardless of account, so a shared browser accumulates every account's projects in a single start-menu list with nothing separating them locally.
pushProject's catch (syncEngine.js:70-75) logs nothing at all, unlike reconcile's per-project console.warn — push failures leave no diagnostic trace whatsoever.
WelcomeGate.js:18-19 reads localStorage during render unguarded; a storage-blocked browser throws into the ErrorBoundary at "/" (pre-existing app-wide idiom, but the gate makes "/" depend on it).
GET /api/projects (projects.ts:110-125) returns every tombstone with no cap on the response, so a churn-heavy account ships ~200 rows (100 live + 100 retained tombstones) to every reconcile.
SyncChip.js:31 keys its engine subscription on the whole `me` object while SyncProvider was narrowed to `[me?.id]` — the chip still resubscribes on unrelated profile-field churn.

SyncChip.js:6 maps engine state `idle` to "Synced" — before any push has been attempted, and again for the instant after `setOnline(true)` flips offline→idle (syncEngine.js:237) while `pending` is still non-empty, the chip asserts "Synced" when nothing has synced.

styles.css:4461 and 4474 hardcode `rgba(255,255,255,0.06)` borders in a themed stylesheet that already has `--border` (#e5e5e5 in light); under [data-theme="light"] the welcome cards (#f3f3f3 on #ffffff) and the playground canvas lose their borders entirely.

styles.css:4433 gives `.welcome-orbit__sun` a hardcoded gold glow `rgba(250,204,21,0.35)` over `background: var(--yellow)`; in light theme `--yellow` is #795e00 (dark olive), so the sun is olive with a bright-yellow halo.

The `pide_guest_import_declined:<userId>` localStorage key is written inline at SyncProvider.js:94 and :181 while every sibling key (SIGNED_IN_HINT_KEY, WELCOME_SEEN_KEY, THEME_STORAGE_KEY) is centralised in constants/index.js, which documents itself as "a single source of truth" for storage keys.

Two directories named for sync — `frontend/src/sync/` (React surface) and `frontend/src/utils/sync/` (engine) — with `SyncProvider` importing from both; easy to mis-import and inconsistent with the flat `welcome/` module.

GuestImportPrompt.js:8 says "into your new account?" but SyncProvider fires it at first sign-in on ANY device (SyncProvider.js:94), so a two-year-old account signing in on a lab machine with guest work is told it is new.

On a partially-failed import accept, SyncProvider.js:169-174 leaves the prompt open with the original `importPrompt.count` (line 95), so a user who imported 2 of 3 is still told "Bring your 3 guest projects".

reconcile runs unthrottled on every window `focus` (SyncProvider.js:129, 136) with no in-flight guard; returning focus from the GlowScript iframe or alt-tabbing flickers the chip syncing→synced and issues a `/api/projects` request each time, and overlapping reconciles can interleave status writes.

syncEngine.js:204/215 `console.warn`s once per project per reconcile; on a captive-portal or flaky school Wi-Fi (navigator.onLine still true) a teacher's devtools fills with one warn per project per window focus.

WelcomePage.js:28 constructs an IntersectionObserver with no capability check; `.welcome-reveal` defaults to `opacity: 0` (styles.css:4487), so if the constructor throws the effect propagates to the ErrorBoundary, and absent `is-on` the feature cards would otherwise stay invisible.
README.md:79 quotes the chip as "(`Synced` / `Waiting for connection`)" — the rendered chip is "Saved on this computer · Synced" and also has `Syncing…` and `Sync error` states not mentioned.

HelpPage.js:503-509 ("Saving your work") still describes only IndexedDB auto-save with no mention of account sync, the status chip, or the guest-import offer, even though the intro Note at line 352 was updated for sync.
mustFix: syncEngine.js:31,37 — pushOne must stamp the pushing account's ownerId, not preserve the stale one; without it the Critical fix leaves meta permanently naming the wrong owner and push-after-save stays silently disabled for those projects.

syncEngine.js:153,173 — add the same ownerId equality check to the tombstone and delete-inference branches while fixing line 210, so the owner gate is uniform across reconcile rather than applied to one branch.

Task 6 minor — "null ownerId meta on first push" (pushOne's `?? null` at syncEngine.js:31/37): once the reconcile owner guard from Finding 1 lands, a meta row with a null ownerId slips straight through it, so pushOne must stamp the reconciling/adopting owner instead of null or the cross-account fix has a hole.
